title: Fake Proton VPN and NordVPN Chrome Extensions Route Users Through Unrelated Proxy Network
content_md: A large network of fake Chrome VPN extensions impersonating trusted brands such as Proton VPN and NordVPN has been found routing users’ browser traffic through a separate SOCKS5 proxy network. Socket’s Threat Research Team identified 737 free VPN and proxy extensions linked to at least 40 Chrome Web Store developer accounts. Of these, 274 extensions impersonated 66 well-known VPN and privacy brands, including Proton VPN, NordVPN, Surfshark, ExpressVPN, Cloudflare 1.1.1.1, AmneziaVPN, and AntiZapret. The campaign had accumulated 75,486 displayed installs, while 516 extensions remained live with 58,318 installs at the time of collection. The operation mainly targets Russian-speaking users trying to access blocked services such as Instagram, ChatGPT, and YouTube. Many listings used Cyrillic names and descriptions, while promising privacy, IP masking, and unrestricted access. Some also falsely claimed endorsements from public figures. Fake VPN Extensions Hijack Traffic Socket analyzed code from 525 extensions. Of the 522 packages collected in bulk, 520 configured Chrome to send browser traffic through the same SOCKS5 infrastructure on port 1082. The extensions use Chrome’s chrome.proxy.settings API with a fixed proxy configuration. Their bypass lists contain only loopback addresses such as localhost and 127.0.0.1.
